milestones.name: T16 control path proven
milestones.objective: Prove the T16 can use its Windows PowerShell and SSH configuration to run a harmless command in T480 Ubuntu WSL and return structured output.

checks.description: T16 PowerShell and Windows OpenSSH are callable from the execution environment.
T16 authenticates to the T480 using an SSH key without a password prompt.
A harmless Ubuntu WSL command on the T480 returns output to the T16.
The T16 adapter executes the real T480 Windows health operation and returns host data.

milestones.name: Docker runtime proven
milestones.objective: Install and verify Docker Engine and the Compose plugin in T480 Ubuntu.

execution_steps.action: Run the read-only Docker status operation.
execution_steps.purpose: Confirm whether Docker already exists and avoid overwriting a runtime.

execution_steps.action: Add Docker's authenticated Ubuntu package source.
execution_steps.purpose: Install supported Docker packages for Ubuntu 26.04 and amd64.

execution_steps.action: Install Docker Engine, container runtime, Buildx, and Compose.
execution_steps.purpose: Provide the runtime required for the lab's Compose services.

execution_steps.action: Enable and start Docker, then add the Ubuntu chris user to the Docker group.
execution_steps.purpose: Make Docker available after WSL starts and usable by the lab operator.

execution_steps.action: Run Docker, Compose, service, and hello-world checks in a fresh Ubuntu session.
execution_steps.purpose: Prove real container execution rather than package presence alone.

checks.description: Docker Engine responds in a fresh Ubuntu session.
Docker Compose plugin responds in a fresh Ubuntu session.
A hello-world container runs successfully.

milestones.name: Lab stack operational
milestones.objective: Run the repository's PostgreSQL and n8n stack privately on the T480.

checks.description: The intended repository revision is present on the T480.
Docker Compose resolves the local configuration successfully.
A T480-captured and independently verified evidence bundle proves PostgreSQL, pgvector, and n8n are healthy.

milestones.name: Recovery proven
milestones.objective: Prove the lab can create and verify a synthetic PostgreSQL backup and restore path.

checks.description: A PostgreSQL backup is created outside the container.
A synthetic restore is completed into the intended test target.
Expected synthetic data is verified after restore.

milestones.name: Hands-off maintenance and recovery proven
milestones.objective: Prove the T16 can govern a planned T480 maintenance cycle, including an unattended Windows restart, boot-time recovery of the private PostgreSQL and n8n stack, Windows Update control, and BIOS-update readiness without storing Windows credentials or enabling automatic logon.

execution_steps.action: Capture T480 power, storage, BitLocker recovery, Windows Update, BIOS version, Docker, database-backup freshness, and service-health state without making changes.
execution_steps.purpose: Refuse unsafe maintenance before any restart, firmware action, or service disruption.

execution_steps.action: Configure a Windows boot-triggered Scheduled Task running as Local System to start Ubuntu WSL, wait for Docker, and start the private PostgreSQL plus n8n Compose services. Do not use Windows automatic logon.
execution_steps.purpose: Make the lab recover after restart without an interactive Windows user session.

execution_steps.action: With explicit approval, restart the T480 from the T16 and poll for its return over the existing authenticated control path.
execution_steps.purpose: Prove the real boot-time recovery path instead of assuming a registered task works.

execution_steps.action: Set and verify a defined maintenance window and active-hours policy, then run one governed Windows quality-update cycle or record authoritative proof that no applicable quality update is pending.
execution_steps.purpose: Keep security updates current without unplanned interruption of the lab.

execution_steps.action: Use Lenovo's supported update tooling to capture the current and offered BIOS versions, release information, AC/battery state, and BitLocker recovery readiness. Do not install firmware as part of this milestone.
execution_steps.purpose: Make a later explicit BIOS-update decision safe and evidence-based.

execution_steps.action: Capture the raw T480 maintenance outputs and independently verify the bundle from the T480 before updating the milestone ledger.
execution_steps.purpose: Keep the ledger as an index while retaining real-machine proof.

checks.description: A T480-captured task definition proves a boot trigger, Local System principal, fixed startup action, and no automatic Windows logon dependency.
After an approved T16-initiated Windows restart and without interactive Windows logon, the T16 reconnects and a T480-captured check proves Docker active plus PostgreSQL and n8n healthy.

T480 evidence proves the configured maintenance window and active hours, and records either a completed quality-update/restart cycle or an authoritative no-applicable-quality-update result followed by service health verification.

T480 evidence records current and offered Lenovo BIOS versions, release reference, AC/battery readiness, BitLocker recovery readiness, and an explicit decision to defer or separately approve any BIOS install.
A raw T480 evidence bundle is independently verified and its manifest fingerprint is recorded in the local ledger.

milestones.name: Governed n8n upgrade proven
milestones.objective: Implement and prove a repeatable, approval-gated n8n security-upgrade lifecycle that moves the T480 from the vulnerable 1.118.1 image to a reviewed, digest-pinned 1.x release at or above 1.121.0, without exposing n8n or losing workflow data.

execution_steps.action: Capture the installed n8n version, the target release notes, applicable security advisory, breaking-change assessment, and the exact official image digest selected for the target 1.x version.
execution_steps.purpose: Make the upgrade decision reviewable and prevent mutable-tag deployments.

execution_steps.action: Create and independently verify a fresh PostgreSQL backup, record the current image digest as rollback reference, verify free capacity, and prove n8n plus PostgreSQL are healthy before changes.
execution_steps.purpose: Protect workflow and credential data before n8n database migrations run.

execution_steps.action: Implement a fixed approval-gated adapter operation that verifies preflight evidence, pulls the selected image, recreates only n8n, waits for health, and returns non-secret version and image evidence. It must not accept a caller-supplied image, command, or tag.
execution_steps.purpose: Provide a safe repeatable upgrade mechanism rather than ad hoc Docker commands.

execution_steps.action: Verify n8n version, image digest, loopback-only port binding, PostgreSQL readiness, and a bounded synthetic workflow execution through the n8n adapter.
execution_steps.purpose: Prove the new image works with the real lab data path, not just that a container started.

execution_steps.action: Document the rollback decision point and execute a controlled rollback only if post-upgrade validation fails. If validation passes, retain the verified backup and rollback image reference without downgrading a migrated database.
execution_steps.purpose: Avoid unsafe downgrade assumptions while retaining a recoverable failure path.

execution_steps.action: Add a read-only release/advisory status check and a recurring maintenance reminder or workflow that reports, but never auto-installs, new n8n security updates.
execution_steps.purpose: Detect future releases while preserving explicit human approval for changes.

checks.description: Evidence identifies the prior and target n8n versions, the reviewed advisory/release rationale, applicable breaking changes, and the exact target OCI digest.
A fresh independently verified PostgreSQL backup and the prior image digest are retained before the n8n container is changed.
A real T480 deployment runs a reviewed digest-pinned n8n 1.x image at version 1.121.0 or later, and n8n is healthy with its port still bound only to 127.0.0.1.
A bounded synthetic workflow executes successfully after the upgrade, with T480-captured raw execution evidence and no production credentials or customer data in the proof.
A read-only recurring release/advisory review reports pending n8n updates without downloading, installing, or activating an image.
A raw T480 evidence bundle covering backup, upgrade, health, and workflow validation is independently verified before the milestone ledger is marked proven.
